1.assumed: Archimedes: upthrust equals the weight of fluid displaced.

2.assumed: Cells, generators and solar cells supply e.m.f.; an LDR only dissipates energy.

3.assumed: Emission is instant above threshold frequency; intensity changes number of electrons not their KEmax.

4.assumed: At terminal velocity drag equals weight; mass in kg; solve for v.

5.assumed: Work against the body removes kinetic energy; speed is proportional to √KE.

6.assumed: On a fixed supply P = V²/R, so the largest total resistance dissipates least power.

7.assumed: Energy stored under Hooke's law = ½ × force × extension.

8.assumed: Strain is unitless, so Young modulus and stress share units of Pa.

9.assumed: Metals have very high carrier number density (~10²⁸ m⁻³); insulators very low.

10.assumed: Longer, thinner wire has larger resistance, changing current and how p.d. is shared.

11.assumed: Double-slit fringes come from diffraction plus interference of the two coherent waves.

12.assumed: ρ = RA/L with A = πd²/4, converting lengths to m.

13.assumed: Count loops in the pattern to find the harmonic number; fundamental = f/n.

14.assumed: p = √(2mE), so doubling KE divides λ by √2.

15.assumed: Phase difference = fraction of a period between points × 360°.

16.assumed: Convert eV to J, find λ = hc/E, then match to the visible range 400–700 nm.

17.assumed: Table headings use quantity / unit; 10⁶ factor in the heading; round to 2 s.f.

18.assumed: Horizontal velocity component u cos θ is constant, so range = u cos θ × t.

19.assumed: Electron diffraction shows electrons behave as waves.

20.assumed: Impulse is the area under a force–time graph.

21(a).assumed: Drops leave at equal time intervals, so growing spacing means increasing speed.

21(b).assumed: An object stays at rest unless a resultant force acts on it.

21(c)(i).assumed: Velocity is the gradient of a tangent to the s–t graph, or use suvat from rest.

21(c)(ii).assumed: Rate of change of momentum = Δ(mv)/Δt, unit N or kg m s⁻².

22(a).assumed: A ruler with mm divisions resolves to about ±1–2 mm.

22(b).assumed: Percentage uncertainties add; a squared quantity doubles; convert back to absolute.

23(a).assumed: Voltmeter across LED, ammeter in series, vary p.d. until it just lights; darken surroundings.

23(b)(i).assumed: Electrons per second = current ÷ electron charge.

23(b)(ii).assumed: Area from diameter (halve, mm to m); solve I = Anev for v.

23(c)(i).assumed: Current heats the NTC thermistor, lowering resistance so its share of p.d. falls.

23(c)(ii).assumed: Series p.d.s add to the supply; same current through both; R = V/I.

24(a).assumed: All EM waves travel at c in a vacuum.

24(c).assumed: Photon energy ∝ 1/λ; number of visible photons = ratio of energies.

25(a)(i).assumed: Sound is longitudinal; only transverse waves can be polarised.

25(a)(ii).assumed: Use a speaker, gap and microphone; sound spreads beyond the gap when its width is comparable to wavelength.

25(b)(i).assumed: Refractive index = speed of light in vacuum ÷ speed in the material.

25(b)(ii)1.assumed: Frequency unchanged; higher n means lower speed so shorter wavelength.

25(b)(ii)2.assumed: Snell's law n₁ sin θ₁ = n₂ sin θ₂.

25(b)(ii)3.assumed: TIR only occurs going into a medium of lower refractive index.

26(a).assumed: Moments balance about the pivot; rod weight = ρALg acting at its centre.

26(b)(i).assumed: Draw a straight best-fit line; large triangle for gradient.

26(b)(ii).assumed: Equate gradient to the expression's coefficient and solve for density.
